name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "The Thr45Met substitution sits on the WH1 surface that contacts WIP, so the bulkier, hydrophobic Met side chain disrupts the WASP\u2013WIP interface without changing the fold.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E15", "E4", "E5", "E8", "E9"], "would_refute": "Residue 45 in PDB 9S9X (WASP/WIP complex) has no atom within about 5 \u00c5 of any WIP atom, and modelling Met at position 45 in that complex leaves the interface contacts and buried surface area unchanged.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "Only residue-specific structural evidence is E15, which observes residue 45 in a WASP/WIP complex, so the residue is at least near a binding partner. This is observation, not proof of contact. The stability scores (E7, E9, E10, E13) are generic to the protein and do not separate fold effects from interface effects. Missing: contact distances in 9S9X, any measured Thr45Met binding or folding data (G1, G4)."}

arguments: {"statement": "The Thr45Met substitution destabilises the WH1 \u03b2-sandwich core: Thr45 packs against neighbouring hydrophobic residues, and the larger Met side chain causes steric clash that lowers folding stability and reduces the fraction of properly folded protein.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E7", "E9", "E10", "E13", "E18", "E11", "E3"], "would_refute": "In the AlphaFold model AF-P42768-F1 and in 9S9X, residue 45 is solvent-exposed (relative accessibility above about 40%) and a Thr-to-Met model with local relaxation gives a predicted stability change under 1 kcal/mol with no change in neighbouring backbone or side-chain positions.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Several predictors (AlphaMissense 0.59, EVE 0.68, popEVE -4.3, conservation 0.62) point to damage, and the neighbouring WH1 mutants L46P and A47D are stable in a complementation assay (E11), which makes a fold-level effect plausible.
